title: After MARS alerts, operators divert production and gas from an Iraqi source in February 2026; UNEP estimates 60,500 tonnes of methane emissions
summary: UNEP records detection of an Iraqi methane source on August 21, 2025 and mitigation on February 25, 2026. It estimates 60,500 tonnes emitted and does not name the operator.
account: UNEP’s original IRQ_S_050 case document records mitigation on February 25, 2026 at an Iraqi oil and gas facility, after first detection on August 21, 2025. Operators diverted production and associated gas to newer infrastructure. The document records two detected plumes and estimates 60,500 tonnes of methane emissions. It was updated on April 15, 2026. The Chemical Engineer’s May 5 report links the source to the Zubair area and reports an Eni leak-detection campaign, but Eni did not confirm closure of this specific source. UNEP’s case document does not name the operator. Satellite non-detection is limited by the instrument’s sensitivity and observation conditions.
purpose: Satellite-based detection and notification of large methane plumes so that operators mitigate them. This case was that purpose.
system: UNEP IMEO Methane Alert and Response System (MARS): satellite plume detection and analysis with AI models, notification and satellite confirmation
deployer: UNEP International Methane Emissions Observatory (notification); facility operators in Iraq (gas diversion); the article names Eni as operator of the Zubair field
location: Zubair oil and gas field near Basra, Iraq (location reported as apparent, not confirmed)
domain: Climate change mitigation / methane emissions monitoring
segment: Oil and gas production; intergovernmental observatory

ratings.reason: Operators are reported to have diverted gas to a newer facility. The operator did not confirm the specific closure, and no operational detail or cost is documented.
Reported as the largest source mitigated in 2026, after an estimated 1.7m tCO2e released since 2023. It is still one case among about 41 confirmed, and unconfirmed by the operator.

fields.account: UNEP’s original IRQ_S_050 case document records mitigation on February 25, 2026 at an Iraqi oil and gas facility, after first detection on August 21, 2025. Operators diverted production and associated gas to newer infrastructure. The document records two detected plumes and estimates 60,500 tonnes of methane emissions. It was updated on April 15, 2026. The Chemical Engineer’s May 5 report links the source to the Zubair area and reports an Eni leak-detection campaign, but Eni did not confirm closure of this specific source. UNEP’s case document does not name the operator. Satellite non-detection is limited by the instrument’s sensitivity and observation conditions.
